Card Title: Elder Intervention
Blood/Pool: 1 blood
Clan/Discip.: n/a
Card Type: Reaction
Card Text: Do not replace until after combat.
Only usable after a bleed against you is declared. This
reacting vampire gets +2 intercept.
Artist: Michael Weaver
Rarity: Common

Card Title: Shadow of the Beast
Blood/Pool: 1 blood
Clan/Discip.: Protean
Card Type: Action
Card Text: If this action succeeds, put this card on the acting
vampire. The vampire gets one optional manuever
each combat. A vampire may have only one Shadow
of the Beast card.
(S) As above, and this vampire gets an optional press
each combat.
Artist: Pete Venters
Rarity: Uncommon

Card Title: Protected Resources
Pool: 2 pool
Clan/Discip.: n/a
Card Type: Master
Card Text: Master
If this card is in play, another Methuselah may not
bleed you for more than 2 pool. Burn this card if you
successfully bleed another Methuselah.
Artist: Richard Thomas
Rarity: Rare

Card Title: Justicar Retribution
Card Type: Political Action
Card Text: Political Card-Worth 1 Vote
Called by any vampire at +1 stealth.
Successful vote burns all vampires with a current
bleed of 3 or more.
Artist: Michael Weaver
Rarity: Uncommon

and as far as I can remember the following cards were also changed:
- Stake is now Wooden Stake as "paralyze" is removed from the game. WS
is basically the same as Stake except all the paralyze stuff is now part
of the card text.
- Gangrel De-evolution is now Gangrel Avatism (still lame).
- Camille Devereux is replaced by Raven (same stats, different picture
and name).
- Dominate Kine is now Kine Dominance.
- Blood Rage correctly printed as a Thaumaturgy card.

I think that's it, but I may have slipped a few...

Messages.Author: Justin Grace
Messages.Body:
In article <337AEA...@dde.dk>, Brian Rasmussen <b...@dde.dk> writes

>Frank wrote:
>>
>> Hi
>>
>> What are the cards that are in V:TES but are not the jyhad? I know Archon
>> Investigation is one but the other two??

That isn't quite my question, but I was wondering whether there was an
official stance on cards like Bonding, Threats and Conditioning which
had a text change between the two - Bonding in Jyhad only refers to
itself, Threats and Conditioning as being unplayable after it - meaning
that you could play a Foreshadowing Destruction. However, the V:TES
version says no further mods meaning it couldn't be played.

Is there an official thing for them because I've checked the errata and
it doesn't make it clear. Are any card changes in V:TES backdated to
Jyhad ie Jyhad Bonding should actually read "No Further Bleed Mods", or
are they played as written?
--
James Coupe

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Justin Grace wrote:
> I was wondering whether there was an
> official stance on cards like Bonding, Threats and Conditioning which
> had a text change between the two - Bonding in Jyhad only refers to
> itself, Threats and Conditioning as being unplayable after it - meaning
> that you could play a Foreshadowing Destruction. However, the V:TES
> version says no further mods meaning it couldn't be played.
>
> Is there an official thing for them because I've checked the errata and
> it doesn't make it clear. Are any card changes in V:TES backdated to
> Jyhad ie Jyhad Bonding should actually read "No Further Bleed Mods", or
> are they played as written?

Yes. The official rule is that all cards are treated as if they
have the latest wording. All cards are played as the latest version
is written (with all applicable errata, of course).



Messages.Author: Pheersum
Messages.Body:


Note that some errata has been added wherever the V:TES card text
differed only in error. For instance Smiling Jack the Anarch was
errataed back to its Jyhad wording when the V:TES version was found to
contain an error causing the card to cost more to the person playing it
than to its victims.
